question: Regulation (EU) 2016/2336 requires the Commission to adopt, on the basis of the best scientific information available, implementing acts to determine the list of areas where vulnerable marine ecosystems (VMEs) are likely to occur. ICES has recognised in its scientific advice that there are many more closures in the south of the EU than in the north as a result of an uncorrected bias, attributed to latitude.
It has also criticised the imposition of buffer zones that are targeted exclusively at trawling (mobile gears), but apply in practice to all gears and have an unfair impact on static gears. 1.
What steps has the Commission taken to address this discrimination between northern and southern regions of Europe, thereby ensuring proportionality and regulatory fairness?
Does the Commission consider it appropriate to apply, even in buffer zones, scientific models designed for mobile fishing gears to other (static) fishing gears to which they are not related?
Does the Commission consider it proportionate to apply closures targeted at trawling to fixed gear in buffer zones that can be up to three times larger than the VMEs to be protected?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (30.5.2024) The Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/16141 (VMEs Regulation) establishes a list of vulnerable marine ecosystems (VMEs) areas, based on the advice of the International Council for the Exploration of the Sea (ICES)2. The scientific basis for the polygons, set by the ICES, is at C-square resolution of 0.05° latitude x 0.05° longitude.

While it is true that the surface of a C-square varies with latitude, because the distance of a degree of longitude decreases from the equator to the pole, this is the resolution in the ICES database and at which the spatial data calls are issued, and is the resolution at which data on fisheries activities is available.

Among the 87 VMEs areas, there are in fact more closures in the North than in the South: 40 polygons in Irish waters, 22 polygons in French waters, 12 polygons in Spanish waters and 13 polygons in Portuguese waters. The 87 VMEs area is 16.419 km2, which represents 17% of the North-East Atlantic deep EU waters (400-800 meters) and 1.16% of the EU waters of the North-East Atlantic.

ICES advises for buffer zones3 as part of the VMEs protection zone. Similar buffer zones are applied in the North-East Atlantic Fisheries Commission (NEAFC) VMEs closures. The ICES buffer zones approach is also applied in Northwest Atlantic Fisheries Organization (NAFO) VMEs closures4. The ICES advice 2021 is not only addressing bottom trawling. It covers all static and mobile gears that touch the seabed.

The intensity of fishing with static gears is more difficult to assess for ICES, but the advice determines where static gears are fishing. In line with the Deep-sea Access Regulation5 read together with the VMEs Regulation, the prohibition to fish below 400 meters applies to all bottom gears6 in VMEs areas.
1 Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/1614 of 15 September 2022 determining the existing deep-

sea fishing areas and establishing a list of areas where vulnerable marine ecosystems are known to occur or are likely to occur. 2 ICES. 2021. EU Request to advise on the list of areas where VMEs are known to occur or are likely to occur and on the existing deep-sea fishing areas (ref. (EU)2016/2336).

3 ICES considers a buffer zone to be ‘a spatial margin of assurance around the VME to avoid adverse impact’ (ICES advice, 2013). 4 NAFO. 2020. Report of the Scientific Council Working Group on Ecosystem Science and Assessment, 17-26 November 2020, https://www.nafo.int/Portals/0/PDFs/sc/2020/scs20-23.

pdf 5 Regulation (EU) 2016/2336 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 December 2016 establishing specific conditions for fishing for deep-sea stocks in the north-east Atlantic and provisions for fishing in international waters of the north-east Atlantic and repealing Council Regulation (EC) No 2347/2002.

6 ‘bottom gears’ means gears deployed in the normal course of fishing operations in contact with the seabed, including bottom trawls, dredges, bottom-set gill nets, bottom-set longlines, pots and traps. (Regulation (EC) No 734/2008).
